message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles by visiting one of the following resources:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Official U.S. EPA air‑quality index (AQI) for all cities, including Los Angeles. | Search “Los Angeles” → see the latest AQI, pollutant breakdown, and health recommendations. |
| **AQICN** (aqicn.org) | Global air‑quality map with real‑time data from local monitoring stations. | Enter “Los Angeles” → view AQI, PM2.5/PM10 levels, and forecast. |
| **Weather.com / AccuWeather** | Weather + AQI overlay. | Look up “Los Angeles” → scroll to the “Air Quality” section. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish daily air‑quality summaries. | Search “Los Angeles air quality today” on their websites. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, the AirNow website usually updates every 15–30 minutes, so it’s the most reliable source for the current AQI. If you need historical data or trends, both AirNow and AQICN provide charts and downloadable datasets.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "How is the air quality in Los Angeles right now?" We need to provide current air quality. We don't have real-time data. We can suggest checking AirNow or local sources. We can also provide general info. There's no function to get real-time data. So we respond with guidance.
